interpretation.A_sensitivity: Reconstruction R2 rises smoothly with A (0.53/0.62/0.69 at A=4/5/6); the fresh AA refit at A=5 (0.616) reproduces the published fixed-corner value (0.590) within reinit noise. The 59% headline is not fragile to the choice of A=5.
interpretation.variance_is_flat: The map's coordinate variance is near-isotropic (top PC only 26.9%, five PCs needed for 80%). The expected variance a Haar-random k-D subspace captures is exactly k/d (=5/8=0.625) regardless of the eigenvalue spectrum; the 500-seed empirical mean is 0.624 (sd 0.042), confirming this. The archetype-5 R^2 of 0.590 sits at the 21th percentile of random 5-D projections — i.e. slightly BELOW a typical random subspace (by 0.034 R^2 units, z=-0.82), not equal to it.
interpretation.correct_framing: Decisive evidence for the T1.2 reframe: archetypes do NOT compete on variance capture and were never meant to. Reconstruction R^2 is the wrong yardstick — a random 5-D subspace captures MORE variance (0.625) than the archetype simplex (0.590), and PCA-5 far more (0.796), yet none provide what the archetypes do: convex, interpretable, clinically-nameable corners with a per-patient simplex membership. Report R^2 only as an honesty check on how much continuum the corners encode, never as a competitive metric.

_correction_note: random_rotation_5 corrected from an unlucky 10-seed estimate (0.590, which spuriously coincided with archetype-5) to the 500-seed mean 0.624 (= analytic k/d 0.625). Conclusion direction changed from 'matches' to 'archetype-5 falls below a typical random 5-D subspace'.
